reviews.summary: `nerva chat -z "prompt"` runs one turn non-interactively and puts only the final assistant text on stdout — whole escape sequences and C0/C1 control bytes stripped, newlines and tabs kept — with every other word on stderr. The prompt resolves the way `nerva send`'s body does (argument, else `-f PATH` where `-` is stdin, else piped stdin) and a terminal is never read, by either spelling: `-f /dev/tty` is refused rather than blocking forever. A prompt over the hub's own 4,096-character `ChatRequest` bound is a usage error before the request, not an HTTP 422 a script reads as a failed turn. The ladder is stated in `--help`: 0 answered · 1 the turn did not complete · 2 usage · 3 no hub · 4 not authorised · 130 interrupted; Ctrl-C returns 130 with one stderr line instead of an uncaught traceback that could spill a partial answer. **The governance clause is implemented against Hermes, not after it:** no flag auto-approves, a turn that queues an action stays queued, and the verb exits 1 naming what to decide with `nerva approvals`; a test asserts the one-shot path issues no decision call at all. **An independent adversarial review (five lenses, no shared context) broke the first version of that clause in one line and the fix is the substance of this row:** the verdict was an exact-string match on the reply, but the hub does not hand `/chat` the agent's reply verbatim — `Orchestrator._synthesize` wraps a single specialist's answer as `[athena]: …` whenever `jarvis` is not among the responders, which is the ordinary routed path — so `-z` exited 0 with a queued approval printed as the answer. Matching is now by containment over the sanitised text, and the table gained the five tool-loop stops it was missing plus a prefix rule for the one the hub builds with an f-string; the drift test imports all ten constants and asserts each is matched both verbatim and wrapped. Sanitising now happens before the verdict, so a reply of pure control bytes is an incomplete turn rather than exit 0 and a blank line. `--usage-file PATH` writes `nerva.chat.usage.v1` atomically on every path including the interrupt, cleans up its temp file when a write fails, survives a field it cannot encode (a warning, never a crash after the answer is already out), says so when given an empty path, and refuses to call a turn completed while naming an approval it left queued. A hub that reports `pending_approvals` in a shape this version cannot read is told so rather than having a string exploded into one fabricated id per character. 51 tests; 23 mutations of the shipped behaviour each turn at least one of them red, including a second atomicity test that fails under a plain truncating write where the original one passed.
reviews.remaining: Two halves of the row are open, and the first is a governance limit worth stating plainly. (1) THE VERDICT STILL RESTS ON THE REPLY TEXT. `ChatResponse` on this base carries `reply` and nothing else, so `pending_approvals` is always empty against the shipped hub and containment matching is the only detector there is. Containment survives the deterministic `[agent]: …` wrapper; it cannot survive the other synthesis branch, where `jarvis.synthesize` re-writes the text through a model — no string in a reply can. The real fix is the hub reporting what the turn queued, which is the sibling slice stacked on this one (`ChatResponse.pending_approvals` + the SSE end event); until that is on main, `nerva chat -z` can still be defeated by an LLM-rewritten refusal, and the CLI's stderr says "this hub did not report the id" rather than naming it. (2) THE SPEND HALF IS A SCHEMA OF NULLS. The hub cannot attribute one turn's cost: `AgentConfig.model` defaults to `google/gemma-4-31b-a4b`, none of the 18 agents in `agents/_system/agents.yaml` declares a model, so `cost_tracker` meters every turn at the default price row and reports $0.00, and an id it does not know is priced from the `default` row with no `priced` flag. `estimated_cost_usd`, the token counts, `api_calls`, `model` and `provider` are therefore `null` with `cost_basis: "unavailable"` rather than measured zeros; a test pins that they never become numbers. Also open: `POST /chat` returns no trace, invocation or session id, so `session_id` is echoed only when the caller supplied one; `-z` does not silence hub-side logging; there is no `--output-format` beyond the existing `--json`; a piped body is read whole up to the bound rather than streamed; and `os.replace` onto a symlinked `--usage-file` path replaces the link with a regular file instead of writing through it.

reviews.summary: `nerva security audit` inventariază distribuțiile interpretorului curent și pinurile Python exacte ale descriptorilor de extensie numiți, întreabă OSV.dev prin `PluginHTTPClient` (rezoluție DNS pinată, ancorele TLS ale owner-ului, breaker; querybatch în loturi de 1000 cu paginare urmărită + un detaliu per advisory; pleacă doar perechi nume+versiune, anunțate pe stderr), unește oglinzile GHSA/PYSEC ale aceluiași CVE într-o singură constatare cu cea mai mare severitate declarată, numește fix-ul din intervalul care conține versiunea instalată și iese 0/1/5. Un advisory fără severitate declarată pică orice prag; o bază de date de neatins, un lot rămas paginat după 20 de pagini sau un audit care nu se încheie înseamnă exit 5 și nicio afirmație. O distribuție cu metadate nedecodabile e sărită și numită; textul advisory-urilor e curățat de caractere de control înainte de terminal. MCP (comenzi stdio configurate de owner) e listat ca neauditat, cu motivul. Probat live: 48 distribuții curate; un pin `requests 2.19.0` dă 5 constatări după unirea a 5 oglinzi PYSEC. Recenzie adversarială independentă: nouă defecte, toate remediate în același PR.
reviews.remaining: Suprafața MCP nu e auditată: comenzile stdio (`npx …`, `uvx …`) din configurația persistată nu sunt rezolvate la pachete și versiuni. Descriptorii de extensie trebuie numiți pe linia de comandă; catalogul pachetelor achiziționate e pe partea hub-ului și nu e citit offline. Nu există `nerva security` implicit (cli-d.security-default) și nici `--skip-venv/--skip-plugins/--skip-mcp`. Vectorii CVSS nu sunt scorați: un advisory doar cu vector rămâne `unknown` și pică orice prag dacă nu se unește cu un frate GHSA evaluat. Pragul implicit `--fail-on low` e deliberat mai strict decât `critical` din Hermes. Nu există setare de proxy pentru operator (H281). Din procesul CLI nu există mediere kernel și registrul de egress nu persistă. Scara de ieșire e cea Nerva (0/1/2/5), nu 0/1/2 din Hermes. Fără probă pe o mașină fără proxy transparent.

reviews.summary: The port-conflict diagnostic, plus one stale line of evidence corrected. `serve.py` gains `probe_bind(host, port)`, called from `main()` after the posture guards and before uvicorn binds: a taken port prints the exact address, the command that identifies the holder (`nerva status`) and the way out (`JARVIS_PORT`), then exits **12**; `EACCES` on a privileged port exits **13**. Both are deliberately distinct from uvicorn's `STARTUP_FAILURE` (3), which it uses for *every* startup failure — that collision was the actual defect, because a supervisor could not tell "the port is taken" from "the lifespan crashed". The probe is a **diagnostic, not a lock**: it binds and closes, reserves nothing, and any `OSError` outside the two named arms is swallowed, so an unexpected probe failure can never turn a boot that would have worked into a refusal. The socket **constructor sits inside the guarded region** too — a first cut that built it above the `try` turned `JARVIS_HOST=::1` on a box with no IPv6 stack into an 8-frame traceback + exit 1 in place of uvicorn's one-line error + exit 3, the diagnostic making the boot worse than no diagnostic. It also mirrors asyncio's own flags rather than stricter ones: `SO_REUSEADDR` on POSIX, because `uvicorn.Server.startup` binds through `loop.create_server` where asyncio sets it, so a probe without it would refuse a port merely holding a TIME_WAIT connection from the instance the owner just stopped — a boot uvicorn would have completed. **The frozen 2026-09-07 evidence was stale on one point**: it recorded "no --status", but `nerva status` has existed since the unified CLI (`agents/cli/nerva.py:101,481`). 9 probe tests, and both exit codes are asserted **by execution** rather than by reading the branch — the `EACCES` arm runs in a child dropped to an unprivileged uid with `setpriv`, because pytest runs as root here and a sub-1024 bind simply succeeds. ENV-122 in `docs/test-manual/01-environment-and-boot.md` moves from a message-quality finding to an asserted string plus exit code.
reviews.remaining: Hermes's row is start, check **and stop**, and the stop half is entirely absent: no `stop` verb, no pidfile, no ready file. The row cites `hermes dashboard --status/--stop` plus backend ready sentinels and a ready file (06-cli-f.md, 16 entries); Nerva has `nerva status`, which reads the HTTP surface and so cannot report a hub that is starting or wedged before the port opens, and Ctrl-C. Hermes also signals the conflict as a machine-readable `BACKEND_PORT_IN_USE`, where this slice signals it as an exit code and an English sentence — enough for a supervisor, not enough for a caller parsing a status stream. Not delivered either: `--isolated`, `--skip-build`, `--no-open`, the SSH session-token file and owner-nonce, or the interactive auth-setup prompt. **One known limit, in the safe direction:** the probe picks a single address family from the host string while uvicorn binds every address `getaddrinfo` returns, so a dual-stack name like `localhost` is probed on v4 only and can miss a conflict held on the v6 address — it misses silently, and uvicorn then reports it exactly as it does today. The Windows half of the `SO_REUSEADDR` choice is read off asyncio's `reuse_address = os.name == "posix"` line and has never been executed here; that test skips off POSIX and the docstring says so. **Adversarial review of this slice found the probe stricter than the bind it predicts, and it is fixed here:** `probe_bind` mirrored asyncio's `SO_REUSEADDR` but not the `IPV6_V6ONLY` it sets six lines below, on every AF_INET6 socket. On Linux with the default `net.ipv6.bindv6only=0` that made the probe a DUAL-STACK bind where uvicorn's is v6-only, so with anything IPv4-only holding `0.0.0.0:<port>`, `JARVIS_HOST=::` exited 12 from a boot uvicorn would have completed — the one thing the docstring forbids, and EADDRINUSE is the arm that exits rather than being swallowed. asyncio's own guard is reproduced character for character. The flag being set is pinned through a recording stub, which runs anywhere; the kernel conflict it prevents is pinned by a second test that SKIPS without an IPv6 stack and has NOT been executed — this box has none, so that half is read off CPython's `base_events.py` rather than observed, exactly as the Windows reuse half already is.

reviews.summary: `nerva prompt-size` există și raportează costul fix per apel, pe componente, cel mai mare primul — offline, fără hub, fără backend, fără nicio cerere: citește personele de pe disc și cere registrului specurile pe care oricum le declară. Exact asta îl face utilizabil pentru întrebarea la care răspunde („cât plătesc înainte să înceapă conversația") pe o cutie unde hub-ul nici măcar nu rulează. `agents/core/prompt_size.py` sparge costul în: câte o linie per persoană de agent găsită pe disc, câte una per unealtă — costată ca **JSON-ul care chiar traversează sârma**, nu ca numele ei, fiindcă un `input_schema` stufos poate cântări cât o persoană întreagă — indexul de skill-uri randat exact cum îl randează `build_prompt`, și schela de tură pe care fiecare cerere o plătește. Numărul pe care raportul îl scoate în față e **podeaua per apel**, nu suma: cele 18 persoane sunt listate separat fiindcă o cerere reală trimite una singură, a agentului rutat. Prima versiune a raportului aduna toate cele 18 și anunța 71,8 % dintr-o fereastră de 32k, când o cerere reală plătește ~6,5 % — un număr greșit e mai rău decât niciun număr, așa că podeaua per apel e ce se citește primul și un test o fixează. Fără agent numit se folosește persoana cea mai grea, deci cifra e cazul realist cel mai prost, nu unul măgulitor; un agent inexistent nu e taxat tăcut pe seama altcuiva. Raportul spune despre el însuși că cifrele sunt estimări din aceeași funcție pe care o folosește bugetul la runtime, și trimite la H673 pentru singura măsurătoare exactă — cea raportată de provider. Ieșire text tabelară sau `--json`.
reviews.remaining: Rândul Hermes cere și componente pe care Nerva nu le are separate azi: „cele trei tiere de prompt" și „user profile" nu există ca blocuri distincte în asamblarea promptului (`Agent.build_prompt` are soul + skills + agent memory + schelă), iar `<available_skills>` e un index Hermes; echivalentul livrat e blocul `Available skills:`. Memoria nu e costată: e per sesiune și variabilă, nu cost fix, iar a o raporta ca „fix" ar fi exact tipul de cifră greșită pe care livrarea asta o evită. Schemele de unelte sunt raportate doar când i se dau: verbul nu bootează un registru, iar pe o cutie fără hub secțiunea lipsește și raportul **spune** că lipsește, în loc s-o raporteze ca zero. Cost per toolset (grupat) nu e implementat, doar per unealtă. Neverificat pe serviciu real: nicio cerere nu a fost trimisă — cifrele sunt estimări comparabile cu bugetul intern, nu contorul unui provider.

reviews.summary: Un mesaj vocal pe Telegram e transcris înainte să-l vadă agentul — echivalentul lui `stt_enabled` din Hermes, și jumătatea care lipsea cu totul: „`rg 'voice' agents/core/channels/telegram.py` → nimic". `InboundVoiceReader` întreabă poarta *înainte* de descărcare (o gazdă fără motor de vorbire nu trage înregistrarea nimănui pe disc degeaba), mărginește octeții, îi trimite prin `BytesIO` direct la decodor — vorbirea nu atinge niciodată discul — și transformă fiecare eșec într-un motiv numit. Santinelele motorului (`[silence]`, `[STT unavailable]`, `[STT error: ...]`) nu ajung niciodată la model ca vorbire. Diferența de design față de `media_reader` e deliberată și e miezul securității: descrierea unei poze e observația unui model despre octeți aleși de altcineva, deci circulă în gardul netrusted; un transcript sunt chiar cuvintele expeditorului, la exact nivelul de încredere pe care l-ar fi avut scrise, deci circulă ca o tură obișnuită. A-l pune în gard ar spune modelului să citească cererea proprie a owner-ului ca date în carantină și ar reclama o protecție care nu e cea care lucrează aici — aceea e filtrul de halucinații (H530).
reviews.remaining: Doar intrarea, doar pe Telegram. Nelivrate din cele 7 intrări ale rândului: `stt_echo_transcripts` (să spună înapoi ce a auzit — util exact când transcrie greșit, dar cere o citire de setări în canal și n-a fost strecurat aici); `/voice` ca mod per-conversație (off / răspuns vocal la mesaj vocal / TTS la fiecare replică); intrarea și ieșirea dintr-un canal de voce pe Discord; consumatorul TTS în flux care începe să vorbească propozițiile terminate cât timp modelul încă generează; și, în general, replici rostite pe canalele de chat. NEVERIFICAT pe servicii reale: suita e ermetică — niciun mesaj vocal Telegram adevărat primit, niciun model Whisper încărcat cu adevărat.

reviews.summary: Poza e acum *citită*, nu doar recunoscută. Un `InboundImageReader` o descrie printr-un VLM dovedit local și predă descrierea în tură; textul dintr-o poză intră ca date, niciodată ca instrucțiuni. Regula de localitate e cea din `screen_locator` aplicată pozei altcuiva: `is_local` derivă exclusiv din `resolve_vlm_config().is_local`, se verifică *înainte* să existe un backend, și încă o dată în `_backend_call` împotriva URL-ului la care chiar s-ar posta — două citiri independente, deci un VLM non-loopback nu primește niciun octet. Descărcarea e mărginită de octeții care chiar sosesc, nu de `file_size` (număr ales de expeditor), iar `file_path` primit de la Telegram e validat înainte să ajungă într-un URL care poartă tokenul botului. Descrierea vine în gardul Wave 5a (`fence_tool_result`), deliberat *fără* datamark — `spotlight` ar înlocui spațiile cu „▁" și ar orbi `detect_injection` la gateway, unde clauza de guvernanță a rândului cere marcajul de taint — și normalizată pe o singură linie, ca o poză cu „<<END UNTRUSTED>>" scris pe ea să nu-și poată închide propriul gard. Legenda nu ajunge niciodată la descriitor: e vorba expeditorului, iar un descriitor care ar citi-o i-ar lăsa pe el să aleagă ce „vede" Nerva. Tura merge pe ușa normală, deci `Gateway._inbound_meta` o marchează `inbound:telegram` și rulează detectorul peste exact ce citește modelul. Mesajele vocale sunt și ele citite acum, dar pe cealaltă cale: un transcript sunt cuvintele expeditorului, deci circulă *fără* gard, ca o tură obișnuită (`inbound_voice`; rândul lui e H071). Descriptorul separă acum `recognises_media` de `reads_media`, cu invariantul verificat la construcție, iar `READABLE_KINDS` e exact `{photo, voice}`.
reviews.remaining: Doar fotografii și mesaje vocale, doar pe Telegram. Nu sunt livrate: audio, video, documentele și stickerele; cache-ul pe disc sub un director de media, ca uneltele de vedere să poată deschide o cale; gruparea rafalelor de poze și debounce-ul pe albume; pinurile de locație și venue; cache pentru media din grupuri observate și din mesaje la care se răspunde; ingestia pe WhatsApp, Discord, Teams, Google Chat și email. `READABLE_KINDS` conține exact `{photo}` și nimic nu intră acolo înainte să existe calea de citire pentru tipul respectiv. Limitare pusă pe hârtie, nu rezolvată: taint-ul nu poate fi urmărit *prin* model — ce se transportă e faptul grosier că tura a citit material netrusted, iar originea `inbound` a canalului e cea care ține o acțiune derivată dintr-o poză în aprobare; `mark_turn_recall_tainted()` nu e chemat aici pentru că ar fi un no-op (escalate-only peste o origine deja netrusted), iar un apel decorativ ar fi un control doar cu numele. NEVERIFICAT pe servicii reale: suita e ermetică — niciun mesaj Telegram adevărat primit, niciun VLM local chemat cu adevărat, `getFile` și descărcarea probate doar contra unui client fals.

Browser HUD, ambient and responsive phone layouts synchronize fixed appearance preferences through a narrow user-guarded Settings DB document. Boot reads never write defaults; stale known values coerce to supported choices. Prefix-scoped immutable edit journals preserve offline changes across tabs, server revision CAS prevents stale writes without Web Locks, and acknowledgements remove exact edits even after unmount. Motion defaults to the OS System preference. Two independent real browser contexts recover saved choices after cache loss. Five fixed local UI font choices now share that normalization, revision and offline journal contract. The HUD applies the body/display override at its root; code and explicitly monospace elements retain their independent font stack. Real root/prefix browser tests verify computed families, persistence in a fresh browser, look independence, offline replay and code font invariance. The separate native application now reads the same owner Settings DB document at boot and foreground entry. Its connection-scoped finite cache, explicit-save hydration epochs and serialized current-record writes prevent stale credentials or appearance from returning. All19 native consumers react without resetting local component state; code fonts remain independent. The accepted cross-client preference contract is implemented; native authoring and a full curated font catalog are not required by this row. Scope remains one configured owner instance. Unsupported native fonts have explicit platform fallbacks; unavailable storage cannot preserve offline choices across process restarts. Native rendering is covered with real React source and host mocks, not device GUI proof.

reviews.summary: H270 stays PARTIAL; the triage's "already equivalent" does not survive contact with the code. Hermes' contract has two halves and Nerva has only one of them. Outbound (what a child inherits) is genuinely stronger than Hermes and is tested: scrub_child_env (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:172-210) is default-deny with SAFE_ENV_PREFIXES (:17-33) plus the three-name JARVIS_CHILD_ALLOWED_ENV (:47-51), covered by tests/test_environment_primitives.py:62,90; STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST/stdio_env_baseline (agents/core/mcp/client.py:101-142) drops a credential-shaped name even when allowlisted (:138), covered by tests/test_mcp_transports.py:349. Inbound (what a surface may persist) does not exist as a policy at all: no ENV_VAR_NAME/WRITE_DENYLIST equivalent anywhere, and none of Hermes' hijack names (LD_PRELOAD, PYTHONSTARTUP, NODE_OPTIONS, GIT_SSH_COMMAND, …) appears in agents/, tests/ or frontend/src/ outside the research docs. Confirmed there is no env writer to gate today: no os.environ assignment in agents/ except the reality harness's JARVIS_STRICT_EGRESS toggle (agents/core/observability/reality_harness.py:685,714); no set_key/dotenv write; agents/core/paths.py:130-134 only copies .env.example verbatim; GET /api/admin/env (agents/core/routers/admin.py:167-179) is read-only and mask-redacted with no PUT; the HUD states it in its own copy (frontend/src/panels/workflows-advanced.tsx:48 "There is NO route to change either"). Nerva's actual config writer is settings_db.put_category (agents/core/settings_db.py:531-563), which UPSERTs only DEFAULTS-declared keys and skips the rest (:546-560), behind validate_category (:509-529) and the 422 at agents/core/routers/admin.py:110-116 — the right shape, but over settings keys, not env names. Three things are nevertheless still owed, so this is not equivalence. (1) The row's own deliverable — a declared-names allowlist at the write boundary, depends_on "the key registry" — is unbuilt, and the rationale defers rather than excludes it ("the moment the config writer lands, this must land with it"). (2) The MCP env boundary is unrefused and untested: MCPServerConfig (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:94-105) sets no model_config, so pydantic's default extra="ignore" SILENTLY DROPS an `env` body key rather than refusing it (verified by probe), and no test pins that to_config (agents/core/mcp/client.py:616-630) and load_from_config (:632-668) never round-trip `env`, while the field it would fill is live: MCPServer.env (:245,:275) → _merged_env (:382-395) → create_subprocess_exec(env=…) (:310). (3) The triage's claim that only the legacy _merged_env path skips the filter is wrong — stdio_env_baseline applies per-server overrides unfiltered in the STRICT path too (:141-142, docstring "Explicit per-server overrides always win"; docs/FLAGS.md:521), and the allowlist itself is behind JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE, off by default, with tests/test_mcp_transports.py:395-399 pinning the default as a full parent-env inherit carrying OPENAI_API_KEY. Also checked and cleared, which the triage never examined: scripts/nerva_import.py IS a setup-flow writer that persists foreign env-var names verbatim (docstring :19, parse_json_tokens :287-292, SecretStore write :701), but _SECRET_NAME_RE (:70) admits only credential-shaped names so no hijack name can pass, and SecretStore names never reach a process env. Tests run: 74 passed across the six relevant files; none exercises an env-var write boundary.
reviews.remaining:
Nerva has no write-side policy for environment-variable names — the row's deliverable (a declared-names allowlist, depends_on "the key registry") does not exist, and the row defers it rather than excluding it. Three concrete items are owed, two of them shippable today against real surfaces:

1. THE REGISTRY (the row's core item, blocked on its stated dependency). No ENV_VAR_NAME allowlist/denylist exists anywhere (grep for ENV_VAR_NAME/ENV_WRITE/WRITE_DENYLIST/writable_env across agents/, scripts/, frontend/src/ is empty), no `config.write` capability kind exists in agents/core/capability_actions.py, and none of Hermes' hijack names (LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, DYLD_*, PYTHONPATH/HOME/STARTUP, NODE_OPTIONS/NODE_PATH, PATH, SHELL, BROWSER, EDITOR, VISUAL, PAGER, GIT_SSH_COMMAND) or posture flags is named in code or tests. When any env/config writer lands, a declared-names allowlist must land in the SAME PR, refusing an undeclared name before authorization — the shape of agents/core/capability_actions.py:143-146 refusing missing_inputs before the authorizer at :156.

2. THE MCP `env` BOUNDARY IS UNREFUSED AND UNTESTED (shippable now). agents/core/routers/mcp.py:94-105 sets no `model_config`, so pydantic's default extra="ignore" makes `POST /api/admin/mcp {"env": {"LD_PRELOAD": "/tmp/evil.so"}}` return 200 and silently drop the key instead of refusing it. The field it would populate is live — MCPServer.env (agents/core/mcp/client.py:245, :275) → _merged_env (:382-395) → create_subprocess_exec(env=…) (:310). Owed: `extra="forbid"` (or an explicit named refusal) on MCPServerConfig, plus tests asserting the route refuses an `env` body and that to_config (:616-630) / load_from_config (:632-668) never round-trip `env`.

3. PER-SERVER `env` BYPASSES THE ALLOWLIST IN BOTH BRANCHES, AND THE ALLOWLIST IS OFF BY DEFAULT. stdio_env_baseline applies overrides unfiltered after the allowlist loop (agents/core/mcp/client.py:141-142; docstring: "Explicit per-server overrides always win"), and the legacy branch does `merged.update(self.env)` with no filter (:394) — so the strict path is not a safe landing zone for an operator-supplied `env` either. Compounding it, JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE is off by default (:119-120; docs/FLAGS.md:521) and tests/test_mcp_transports.py:395-399 pins the default as a full parent-env inherit carrying OPENAI_API_KEY. Owed: run per-server overrides through the same name policy (or make the bypass an explicitly reviewed, audited exception), and decide whether the baseline should become the default. Severity, checked directly rather than inferred: the bypass is LATENT today. `MCPServerConfig` has no `env` field at all, `to_config` (:616-630) does not export `env` and `load_from_config` (:632-668) does not read it, and the only production caller that passes an override is Nerva's own WorldView writer with an in-repo secret (agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py:200-206). No untrusted input reaches the override loop, so this is a boundary to close before `env` becomes operator-settable, not a live hole.

reviews.summary:
Both ideas the row said were "worth taking and cheap" are shipped, proven and correct, and the audit's 2026-09-07 nerva_evidence did undersell Nerva — but the row is not equivalent, because the cron half of Hermes' contract has unmet clauses that last night's triage never looked at.

Shipped and verified. The claim lease with a TTL is `autonomy.running_ttl_seconds` (agents/core/settings_db.py:297, default 3600), resynced every coordinator tick (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:265-269) and enforced by `TaskQueue.reap_stuck_running` (agents/core/autonomy/queue.py:1599-1629) through `AutonomyWorker._reap_stuck` (agents/core/autonomy/worker.py:489-503), called first in `tick` (worker.py:889-891). The crash-grace window is the same mechanism, and it satisfies the row's governance note exactly: the reaper FAILS the stranded row with `result.error="stuck_running_ttl"` + `stuck_since` and audits `autonomy.reaped` — it never re-queues, so an already-authorized action is never re-executed. Proven by tests/test_q6_autonomy_killswitch_scope_reaper.py:91-135 and manual case GOV-224 (docs/test-manual/07-autonomy-governance.md:617). The jobs lane carries the same property independently: a manual request found `running` with its cross-process gate free is recorded `unknown` / "execution interrupted after claim; not replayed" (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:172-178), proven by tests/test_job_dispatch.py:130. Beyond the reaper, the scheduled lane has a 64-stripe cross-process file gate every firing must hold (jobs_dispatch.py:33-48 via jobs.py:1097-1105), an identity fingerprint that voids a claim if the job was edited after acceptance (jobs_dispatch.py:14-17, 148-153; jobs.py:1117-1121), APScheduler `max_instances=1`, a workdir allowlist (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_workdir.py), estop/kill-switch seams (jobs.py:1126-1131, worker.py:893-904) and a validated media deadline `jobs.media_send_timeout_seconds` (settings_db.py:226/485, jobs_media.py:18/257).

Correction to the triage on the claim CAS: `claim_mediated` (queue.py:1240-1311) returns None unless `mediation_mode == "enforce"` (queue.py:1243), and `resolve_task_mediation_mode()` defaults to "off" with `JARVIS_TASK_MEDIATION` unset — orchestrator.py:553-556 calls it "shipped dark". In the default posture the worker claims with a bare `transition(task.id, RUNNING)` (worker.py:925-927), and `transition` (queue.py:1459-1497) validates only the status edge, with no compare-and-swap on `mediation_execution_id`. The triage's "a second claimant cannot win" is true only with mediation enforced.

What is still owed, and why this is partial. Hermes' text names seven CRON_* clauses; the triage addressed none of them. (a) There is no per-run wall clock on the plain cron path: `_fire_once` → `_execute` → `_ask`/`_brief`/`_deliver` (jobs.py:1107-1163, 1209-1230, 1351-1412) contains no `asyncio.wait_for` anywhere, while the script path already has exactly that pattern at jobs_scripts.py:405 (120 s) and :455 (30 s). The model call is bounded inside the orchestrator, but the channel send is awaited bare, so a hung adapter holds the gate stripe and the `max_instances=1` slot indefinitely. (b) `JARVIS_TASK_MAX_SECONDS` defaults to 0 = unbounded (executor.py:39-42, autonomy_coordinator.py:1039-1042), so out of the box the only bound on a hung in-process task is the 3600 s reaper — the triage flagged this itself and then filed it as "not this row"; HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT is the first line of this row's contract. (c) The jobs store opens sqlite with neither `timeout=` nor `PRAGMA busy_timeout` (jobs.py:508-511), against the task queue's 30 s of both (queue.py:212-214), so jobs.db writers fall back to SQLite's 5 s default on a WAL shared by the gateway drain loop and cron firings — the _SESSION_DB_TIMEOUT clause, unmet. The delivery-destination knobs are excluded by the row's own rationale and are not counted against it (and are in fact covered anyway by per-job `channel`/`deliver` plus `AUTONOMY_OWNER_CHAT_ID` / `autonomy.owner_chat_id`, jobs.py:1351-1406). The ~14-knob Kanban board remains a product decision, not a slice.

472 tests pass across the scheduled/queued surface with zero failures.
reviews.remaining:
Three cron-lane clauses of Hermes' contract are unmet; the Kanban claim-lease and crash-grace asks are done.

1. HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT — no per-run wall clock on the plain cron path. `JobRunner._fire_once` → `_execute` → `_ask`/`_brief`/`_deliver` (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1107-1163, 1209-1230, 1351-1412) has no `asyncio.wait_for` at any level; in particular `_send_tracked`/`_send` (jobs.py:1379-1412) awaits the channel adapter bare, so a hung Telegram/Discord send holds the job's gate stripe (jobs_dispatch.py:33-48) and its APScheduler `max_instances=1` slot with nothing to break it. The script path already does this correctly — `asyncio.wait_for(self.runner._ask(...), 120)` at agents/core/autonomy/jobs_scripts.py:405 and `asyncio.wait_for(self.runner._send_tracked(...), 30)` at :455 — so the fix is to apply the same bound (ideally a `jobs.run_timeout_seconds` setting alongside the existing `jobs.media_send_timeout_seconds`) to the cron path, recording the overrun as a normal failed run through `_failed` so the 3-strike pause and the incident path still apply.

2. `JARVIS_TASK_MAX_SECONDS` defaults to 0 = unbounded (agents/core/autonomy/executor.py:39-42, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1039-1042), so out of the box a hung in-process queued task is bounded only by the 3600 s stuck-running reaper. Give it a non-zero shipped default (or promote it to a validated `autonomy.*` setting like `running_ttl_seconds`), with a test asserting the default is finite.

3. HERMES_CRON_SESSION_DB_TIMEOUT — the jobs store opens sqlite with neither `timeout=` nor `PRAGMA busy_timeout` (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:508-511), unlike the task queue's `timeout=30.0` + `PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000` (agents/core/autonomy/queue.py:212-214). jobs.db writers therefore fall back to SQLite's 5 s default on a WAL shared by the gateway drain loop and cron firings. One-line parity fix.

Out of scope, not gaps: the delivery-destination knobs (_AUTO_DELIVER_PLATFORM / _CHAT_ID / _THREAD_ID, TELEGRAM_CRON_THREAD_ID) are excluded by the row's own rationale; the residual ~14-knob multi-agent Kanban board (_BOARD / _WORKSPACES_ROOT / _ATTACHMENTS_ROOT / _GOAL_MODE / _DISPATCH_IN_GATEWAY) is a product decision about whether Nerva grows a shared task board, not a slice of this row.

It is enforced at three boundaries, not one: the offering boundary (agents/core/tool_profiles.py:199,206 `allowed = allows(name) and _posture_allows(...)`, narrowed again by agents.yaml patterns at :207-208), the runtime filter before and after the profile (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:245-253), and RPC intake ahead of preflight and handler (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:269-271, reason `job_toolset_not_allowed`). Store boundary: agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:350 lists the option, :353-357 validates it and refuses it with `no_agent`, validate_action:297-298 refuses it on non-`ask` actions, and create/edit both re-resolve (:1041, :1062). Fire time: jobs.py:1242-1244 `with toolset_scope(self._toolset_names(job.options)), selection_scope(job.options)`. Doctor reports the catalog, each job's `toolset_upper_bound` and a `toolsets_unavailable` problem (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_health.py:51-55, :113). Reachable from the CLI (`--toolsets default|none|<ids>`, agents/cli/nerva.py:175,185,893-899) and the HUD (frontend/src/panels/job-builder.tsx:35-49); PATCH /api/jobs/{id} refuses an unavailable toolset with 422 (tests/test_job_toolsets.py:327-328). Hermes' two removal rules are met structurally: I enumerated every register_tool on the production server (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:428-728 plus :741-825 installing file_*, session_search, web_search/web_extract, search_memory and execute_code) and none creates a job, no `schedule.create` kernel capability exists, and none is a messaging/clarify tool that needs a live human. Verified green: 27 cases in tests/test_job_toolsets.py, 28 in tests/test_job_model_pins.py, 306 in the wider related batch (0 failures), and 21 HUD cases in frontend/src/panels/job-toolsets.test.tsx + jobs.test.tsx. What keeps the row open is the contract's second half: a job cannot pin reasoning effort. Selection carries only model/provider (agents/core/llm/job_selection.py:21-25), validate_options rejects any unknown option (jobs.py:350) so the pin cannot be stored, and _ask never enters `reasoning_scope`, so every scheduled run inherits the global `llm.reasoning_effort` / `reasoning_effort_overrides` read in agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:338,351,379,398-399 — while the closed-lifetime transport machinery already exists and is entered only by the live chat path (agents/core/llm/request_context.py:44-79; agents/web.py:1074,1113). reviews.summary: `nerva send` trimite un mesaj către o destinație configurată fără apel de model, cu corpul rezolvat ca la Hermes: argumentul MESSAGE, altfel `-f PATH` (`-` citește stdin), altfel ce e legat pe stdin — un terminal nu e citit niciodată, nici cu `-f -`; un stdin închis e eroare de utilizare, nu traceback; se citește cel mult limita plus un caracter, iar un BOM UTF-8 e eliminat. `-s LINE` e un subiect pe o singură linie *imprimabilă* (orice caracter de control sau separator de linie Unicode e refuzat), purtat de ntfy ca titlu nativ — ASCII imprimabil, cel mult 120, refuzat cu motiv în loc să fie trunchiat tacit de adaptor — și de celelalte canale ca prima linie (subiect, linie goală, mesaj — forma Hermes); `-q` nu tipărește nimic la succes; `--list CANAL` filtrează țintele: un nume care nu poate fi canal direct-send e eroare de utilizare decisă offline, iar un canal pe care un hub mai vechi nu-l listează e exit 1 cu ce listează numit; un argument MESSAGE gol înseamnă „fără mesaj” și cade pe `--file`/stdin. Scara de ieșire e declarată în `--help`: 0 trimis · 1 nelivrat (hub-ul a refuzat sau transportul a eșuat) · 2 utilizare · 3 fără hub · 4 neautorizat. Un fișier binar la `-f` e refuzat cu îndrumarea pentru atașamente, fără să-i reflecte octeții; limita de 4.000 de caractere e regula seam-ului (`carried_length`: subiectul contează unde devine prima linie, nu la ntfy) și CLI-ul aplică aceeași regulă înainte de orice cerere; șirurile venite de la hub sau tastate sunt curățate de caractere de control înainte de terminal. `POST /api/channels/send` primește `subject` opțional (o linie, ≤200), iar seam-ul outbound aplică limita la ce se livrează efectiv. Rate-limit-ul și înregistrarea în IntentLog rămân pe drum. O recenzie adversarială independentă a găsit cincisprezece probleme (două majore: două pin-uri existente din `tests/test_nerva_send.py` rupte), toate remediate în același PR, fiecare cu test.
reviews.remaining: Atașamentele `MEDIA:<path>` nu sunt purtate: o rută care citește căi locale și le trimite pe un canal e egress de fișiere și trebuie să ajungă în spatele Action Kernel-ului, cu un director-sursă delimitat, înainte să existe. Cerința structurală „fără gateway pornit” rămâne o divergență documentată: `nerva send` trece prin hub ca să existe IntentLog și rate-limit. Corpurile peste 4.000 de caractere sunt refuzate, nu fragmentate (Hermes fragmentează per platformă). Slack și Discord rămân reply-only (restul H018); email-ul e exclus deliberat. Nu există adresare `platform:chat_id[:thread]` / `platform:#canal` ca la Hermes: `--channel telegram` înseamnă întotdeauna chat-ul owner-ului. Precedența diverge deliberat: la Hermes argumentul câștigă în fața `--file`, aici ambele deodată e eroare de utilizare. Erorile nu au prefixul `hermes send:`. `JobRunner._send` își păstrează propria rezolvare a destinației (lot-ul jobs). Fără probă live pe un canal real din această sesiune: verificarea a fost prin hub fals și prin ChannelManager-ul real cu adaptoare false.

reviews.summary: The logging half of the row, and only that half. `agents/core/security/log_redaction.py` adds `SecretRedactionFilter`, a `logging.Filter` that runs every record's message and its `args` through `SecretScanner.redact` before a handler can write it. The enable flag is snapshotted at import, so an agent-authored mid-session write to `JARVIS_LOG_REDACTION` cannot turn it off — Hermes's `_REDACT_ENABLED` rule, ported deliberately. A cheap length/substring pre-check runs before any regex (≈8.75 µs per clean record, ~1.9× faster than the full scan; the builder's report said 17.22 µs and ~2.1×, which did not reproduce and is corrected here). `setup_logging()` installs it. **Two majors found by an independent review and fixed before landing:** the module's own docstring tripped the AUD-14 raw-env-read ratchet — the prose contained a literal `os.environ[...]` subscript and the ratchet greps file text line by line, so `tests/test_o26_p2_env_config.py` was RED in the delivered tree; and `install_log_redaction()` walked only the root logger's handlers, while `uvicorn` and `uvicorn.access` set `propagate=False` and own theirs, so the production HTTP server's own access and error logs — the ones that carry an `Authorization` header — were structurally unreachable. `install_log_redaction_everywhere()` now covers every handler owned by any logger in `logging.Logger.manager`, and a test drives a real uvicorn `dictConfig` and asserts a key in an access line is masked. Three minors fixed with it: the length floor was defeated by an extra pattern whose NAME collided with a built-in (it now matches by regex SHAPE, one-to-one, and fails closed on any mismatch); an ordinary `%`-format bug was being swallowed into a bare `[redaction-unavailable]` instead of logging's loud diagnostic (now `[log-format-error]` with the message, args and exception, all scanned first); and the test fixture destroyed an ambient `JARVIS_LOG_FILE` for the rest of the session. 47 tests, each fix red-proofed by neutering it. **Follow-up in the same PR:** the blocking bandit gate flagged both swallowed exceptions as NEW findings. Only the filter's last-ditch blank was suppressed (`# nosec B110`, with its reason); `_cover`'s per-handler swallow became a counted, warned coverage figure and `_managed_loggers`' registry-walk failure became a warning, closing the gap this row disclosed. 52 tests.
reviews.remaining: This is one of the row's seven paths. Hermes applies `redact.py` to logs, verbose output, tool output, approval prompts, gateway messages, transcripts and memory; this slice covers LOGS. Still owed, and the rationale calls them the part that matters most: the hash-chained audit DB (a `cat .env` from `terminal_run` still writes a live credential into an append-only log that by design cannot be edited), the decision-inbox approval card the owner reads on a phone, task payloads, terminal output, and the observability exports — which Hermes scrubs unconditionally with no knob, returning `[redaction-unavailable]` rather than raw text. Also absent: the second mask mode (a syntactically INVALID `«redacted:ghp_…»` sentinel for file reads, so an agent cannot write a masked-but-plausible key back and silently kill the credential), `code_file=True` sparing source constants, `_mask_control_split_tokens()` for tokens smuggled across ANSI/zero-width characters, and the shared `.env` basename list. The two silent-degradation paths named at review are now CLOSED, after the SAST gate forced the question: a handler whose `addFilter` fails is counted and published through `uncovered_handler_count()` and a warning naming how many handlers are writing unredacted, and a `loggerDict` walk that raises warns that coverage fell back to root-only. The one silent swallow left is the filter's own last-ditch blank (`# nosec B110`), where a `logging.Filter` that raises would take down the caller's log call and the scanner has already failed. `install_log_redaction()` remains exported although the `everywhere` variant is what production uses.

Refusal logging is rate-shaped (:657-659, :690) and logs only a coarse peer trust class (:662-671), never the attacker-chosen header value. What keeps this off "equivalent" is the residual the code names about itself at agents/web.py:654-656: _PROBE_PATHS is exempt from the guard (:678-679), so `Host: evil.test` returns 200 on /healthz and /metrics and reaches the route on /readyz. I confirmed live that a rebound page therefore still reads the full 1126-byte Prometheus body (route templates, request counters, latency buckets) and the /readyz body naming the configured LLM backend and the agent/channel counts — cross-origin, because rebinding makes the browser treat them as same-origin. That is low severity and a deliberate operability trade, not an oversight, but it is a real deviation from Hermes' clause as written (which has no carve-out) and it is shippable work, so the row is partial rather than equivalent.
reviews.remaining: The Host guard exempts _PROBE_PATHS (agents/web.py:625, applied at :678-679), so /healthz, /readyz and /metrics answer a rebound name: live-verified, `Host: evil.test` returns 200 on /healthz and /metrics and reaches the route on /readyz, while every real API route returns 400. Because DNS rebinding makes the browser treat those responses as same-origin, an attacker page still reads the full Prometheus body (route templates, request counters, latency buckets) and the /readyz body naming the configured LLM backend and the agent/channel counts. The code names this residual itself at agents/web.py:654-656 ("a rebound page can therefore still read the golden-signal counters"). Close it by narrowing the exemption rather than removing it — the operability reason for it is sound. Suggested shape: keep /healthz and /readyz exempt but strip /readyz's detail to a bare ready/not-ready when the Host is not accepted, and require an accepted Host for /metrics unless the request is unambiguously non-browser (no Origin and no Sec-Fetch-Site, or an explicit JARVIS_METRICS_ALLOW_ANY_HOST opt-in for a monitor that scrapes by an unlisted name). Needs a test alongside test_healthz_from_any_host_is_exempt asserting that a refused Host cannot read the counter body.

reviews.summary: Whisper nu tace când nu aude nimic — inventează. Pe liniște întoarce o propoziție fluentă din datele de antrenament: generice de subtitrare („Subtitles by the Amara.org community", „Subtitrarea: ..."), formule de încheiere („Thanks for watching!", „Mulțumesc pentru vizionare!"). Pentru o casetă de dictare e o enervare; aici e un control de siguranță, exact cum spune clauza de guvernanță a rândului: un mesaj vocal devine o tură *inbound*, o tură inbound poate cere lucruri, deci un transcript halucinat e o instrucțiune pe care n-a autorizat-o nimeni, intrată într-un sistem guvernat. `hallucination.py` o oprește. Designul e dictat de asimetria erorilor: a pierde un mesaj real e inacceptabil (cineva zice „mulțumesc" și dispare fără răspuns), a lăsa unul să treacă costă o tură ignorabilă. De aici două niveluri, nu o listă: frazele distinctive (`CANNED`) cad pe text; cele pe care oamenii chiar le spun (`AMBIGUOUS`) cad doar când durata *decodată* arată că înregistrarea era prea scurtă ca să le conțină — iar un apelant care nu știe durata le păstrează. Potrivirea e pe transcriptul întreg, niciodată pe substring; regula pentru generice cere marker ȘI vocabular exclusiv de generic, fiindcă prima variantă (doar markerul) mânca „am văzut pe amara.org un film bun". Filtrul rulează în `STTEngine.transcribe` și întoarce `[silence]` — santinela care exista deja și pe care fiecare apelant o tratează ca „nu s-a spus nimic" — deci ruta de dictare din browser o primește gratuit, nu doar calea nouă de pe Telegram. CORECTARE la auditul din 07.09: verdictul „missing" era pe jumătate greșit. A doua cerință a rândului — auto-stop pe liniște (VAD), ca utilizatorul să nu apese o tastă — EXISTĂ de mult în `frontend/src/voice.ts`: `recordUtterance` eșantionează RMS la 60 ms și oprește după `SILENCE_MS`, cu plafon dur și abandon când nimeni nu vorbește. Auditul a dat un `rg -i 'vad'` peste `frontend/src/` și a raportat „nimic relevant"; linia 111 spune „VAD" în litere. Ce lipsea cu adevărat era dovada: nimic nu o testa, fiindcă harness-ul comun folosește un MediaRecorder care se oprește singur și scurtcircuitează intervalul. `voice-vad.test.tsx` folosește unul care NU se oprește niciodată singur — dacă o tură se termină acolo, doar detectorul de liniște a putut-o termina — și acoperă fereastra de liniște, plafonul, abandonul și faptul că vorbirea continuă resetează ceasul.

H557 is PARTIAL, not missing and not equivalent. The 2026-09-07 verdict is stale on one half and still correct on the other; the overnight triage's "already equivalent" is wrong.

SHIPPED (the row's rationale half). The name-collision correctness bug is fixed and tested: agents/core/mcp/client.py:566-594 `MCPManager._resolve` accepts a bare tool name only when exactly one server offers it and otherwise returns `{"error": "ambiguous_tool", "servers": [...]}`; `server/tool` or an explicit `server=` pins the server; `find_tool` (client.py:597) and `call_tool` (client.py:606) both route through it; `MCPTool.qualified_name` (client.py:230-233) is the `server/tool` form. tests/test_mcp_hardening.py:41-73 proves first-wins is gone (3 tests, passing). This is a genuine different-spelling equivalent of Hermes' disambiguation property, so `missing` under-reports the row.

NOT SHIPPED (the row's headline half). There is no `_normalize_mcp_input_schema` equivalent. agents/core/mcp/client.py:402-417 `_list_tools` still stores `t.get("inputSchema", {})` verbatim (client.py:410) into `MCPTool.input_schema` (client.py:220) with zero repair — the 2026-09-07 evidence sentence is still literally true. Nerva repairs at the dialect boundary instead, and only for ONE of four providers: agents/core/llm/tool_dialects.py:369-437 `gemini_schema` covers Hermes' `required`-pruning (:423-427) and missing-`type` coercion (:419, :427), and :441-452 avoids the empty-OBJECT 400. The Anthropic path (tool_dialects.py:147-151) and both OpenAI paths (tool_protocol.py:19-27 `as_openai`, responses.py:72-81) pass `input_schema` through byte-for-byte. Two of Hermes' five repairs are absent on every path: I ran the code and confirmed `gemini_schema({"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"null"}],"default":null})` → `{"default": null, "anyOf": [{"type":"string"}, {}]}` (the Pydantic null branch is not collapsed, it degenerates to an empty schema), and `{"definitions":{"Node":…},"properties":{"node":{"$ref":"#/definitions/Node"}}}` → `{"properties":{"node":{}}}` (draft-07 `definitions`/`$ref` are not promoted to `$defs`, the referenced shape is silently deleted). No name sanitization exists anywhere: `grep -rn "mcp__" agents/` is empty, and `qualified_name`'s `/` is not a legal provider function-name character.

ON REACHABILITY. The triage is right that this is currently unreachable from a model: `MCPManager.get_tools()` (client.py:560-564) has zero callers in the whole repo, `MCPTool.input_schema` is read nowhere outside its constructor, and agents/core/routers/mcp.py:71-79 and :193-194 expose only name/description/read_only to the HUD, never the schema. But the triage's grep was scoped wrong and missed a real production consumer of the dispatch path: agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py:141 calls `self.mcp.call_tool(tool, mcp_args)` by bare name (it lives inside agents/core/mcp/, which their grep excluded). So `_resolve` is not dead code, and its bare-name path is live today.

Unreachability is a reason the remaining work is small and belongs inside the bridge PR — it is not a reason to record the row as done. Six of Hermes' nine clauses are unsatisfied or satisfied on only one of four provider paths, and no test anywhere exercises repair of a third-party `inputSchema`. Recording `equivalent` would put a false claim on a public status page; `partial` with a named remainder is the honest row.
reviews.remaining: No provider-agnostic repair of a third-party MCP server's JSON Schema exists. (1) `agents/core/mcp/client.py:402-417` `_list_tools` still stores `inputSchema` verbatim (`:410`); add a `_normalize_mcp_input_schema` applied at registration. (2) Two of Hermes' five repairs are absent on every path, verified by running the code: draft-07 `definitions`/`#/definitions/...` are never promoted to `$defs`/`#/$defs/...` (and `gemini_schema` silently reduces a `$ref` property to `{}`, deleting the shape), and a Pydantic nullable union `anyOf:[{...},{"type":"null"}], default:null` is never collapsed to its non-null branch (`gemini_schema` yields `anyOf:[{"type":"string"},{}]` with `default:null` retained — the exact shape Anthropic 400s on). (3) The three repairs that do exist (`required` pruned to declared names, missing `type` coerced, empty-OBJECT avoided) live only in `agents/core/llm/tool_dialects.py:369-452` and therefore apply to Gemini alone; `anthropic_tools` (tool_dialects.py:147-151), `ToolSpec.as_openai` (tool_protocol.py:19-27) and the Responses payload (responses.py:72-81) pass `input_schema` through unrepaired. (5) The row's security property — a third-party tool shadowing a built-in governed tool name — is unaddressed: `_resolve` disambiguates only among MCP servers, never against the agent tool registry. (6) No test covers any of this; `grep -rln "gemini_schema" tests/` returns only tests/test_cloud_tool_turns.py, and nothing tests `MCPTool.input_schema`. All of the above is currently unreachable by a model because no MCP-client -> tool-registry bridge exists (`MCPManager.get_tools()` has zero callers repo-wide), so the normalizer plus its tests should land inside whichever PR first offers MCP client tools to the model, not as a standalone pure function.
